concept.title: Maintaining and upgrading plug-ins
concept.shortdesc: A plug-in that uses the DITA-OT extension mechanism can usually move to a new DITA-OT release with little work. Automated tests, small overrides and a record of what you changed make each upgrade faster and safer.

section.title: Upgrade checklist
section.p: When a new DITA-OT release is available:

ol.li: Read the release notes and the topic for the release. Note any changes to templates, attribute sets, parameters or extension points that your plug-in uses.

Test the plug-in with the new release:
If you use a CI matrix, add the new version to it, as described in . With the Gradle build from , you can also run the tests locally with ./gradlew dev -PditaOtVersion=version.
Otherwise, install the plug-in into a clean installation of the new release with dita install, check that its transformation types appear in the output of dita transtypes, and run your test transformations.
Compare the output with the output of the previous release, and review the differences.
Update the overrides that no longer match the core code. Check that the require dependencies in plugin.xml still resolve, as described in .
Publish a new plug-in release, and state which DITA-OT versions it has been tested with.

section.note: To replace a version of your plug-in that is already installed, add the --force option: dita install plug-in-zip --force.

section.title: Keep overrides small
section.p: Most upgrade problems come from copies of core code. Override only the templates and attribute sets you need, as described in . Small overrides are easier to compare with the core code, and fewer of them can break when the core changes.

section.title: Track changes to core code
section.p: If your plug-in copies or overrides core files, record which DITA-OT version each copy came from. When you upgrade, compare the new core file with the recorded version to see which of your changes still apply.

section.title: Decide which versions to support
section.p: Each supported DITA-OT version is another version to test. Keep the list short, and keep it in one place, such as the matrix in your CI workflow, so that the versions you test and the versions you document as supported stay the same. When you stop supporting a version, remove it from the matrix and from the documentation.

section.title: Distribute the plug-in
section.p: Package only the plug-in files, in the standard plug-in structure, so that users can install the ZIP file with one command. Keep test content and build files out of the package. See for a project layout that separates them. Keep a changelog, so that users can see what changed between releases.
